title: Hotel Strike Early-Warning for Event Planners
one_liner: A subscription database and parametric cover that tells meeting and group planners which contracted hotels' labour contracts expire before their event, and pays out if a strike hits.
customer: Association and corporate meeting planners, incentive houses, sports and event organisers and tour operators that contract 100+ room-night blocks 12-24 months ahead.
problem: Chicago hotel workers authorised a strike at 85%, potentially the largest in the city's history, and a Seattle Hilton strike lasted 85 days. Planners contract blocks years ahead and learn about labour risk from the news. Strike coverage under contract clauses is vague, and relocating an event on short notice costs heavily.
solution: Track union contract expirations, strike votes and bargaining status per property, from union pages, filings and news. Score each hotel and date for strike risk, alert planners, and provide a labour-disruption clause template. Later add parametric cover underwritten by an MGA that pays per room-night if a strike affects a contracted property.
why_now: Hotel labour unrest is elevated in 2026, hotel costs have repriced sharply, and hotel operators are cutting staff citing AI (Mews cut 15%). Planners are more exposed to relocation than ever.
revenue_model: USD 3-8K per year per planning team, cover premiums of about 1.5-3% of block value, and broker fees.
non_obvious_insight: A strike is a scheduled event, not a surprise. Contract expiry dates are public, yet the buyers of long-dated blocks bear the tail risk and nobody prices it.
first_30_days: Compile a spreadsheet of union contract expirations for the top 40 US convention cities from union local sites and news. Publish a free '2027 events at risk' report to planner communities, then convert responders to a USD 2K annual subscription. Line up an MGA for the cover after the first 10 customers.

title: Payment-Slip Doctor for Foreign Residents
one_liner: A LINE service that lets a foreign resident photograph a Japanese payment slip or government letter and get a plain explanation, deadline, consequences and payment help in their own language.
customer: Japanese-language schools, vocational schools and universities with many foreign students, at about ¥300 per student per month. Later customers are municipal national-health-insurance departments paying for improved collection, employers of foreign staff, and rent-guarantee and property-management firms.
problem: Foreign residents paid on average only 63% of national health insurance premiums by the end of 2024, according to a survey of about 150 local governments. From around FY2027, unpaid premiums and pension contributions will be a ground to deny visa renewal or change of status. Yet at my counter, foreign customers regularly hand me a slip or official letter and ask what it means. The barcode on a konbini payment slip is void after the due date, so I have to refuse it. Then a worker who cannot get to the ward office in daytime faces an arrears spiral that may end in a denied visa. The government mails a notice in Japanese that looks like junk mail.
solution: Photograph the slip or letter. The service reads the barcode and text, identifies the document type such as national health insurance, resident tax, pension or traffic fine, and explains in Vietnamese, Nepali, Chinese, Burmese or Indonesian what it is, how much, when due, and the consequences of non-payment. It sets calendar reminders and links to pay by PayPay, bank app or konbini. If the slip is expired, it generates a reissue script and shows ward-office hours and the nearest late-opening branch. Anything ambiguous or legal is escalated to a partner administrative scrivener. Stickers with a QR code at konbini payment counters are the acquisition channel.
why_now: The 2026 system upgrades that will link municipal payment records to Immigration Services Agency data, plus the rule that unpaid premiums will block renewals from around 2027, make payment compliance a visa issue for hundreds of thousands of students and workers. The current government has made foreign-resident rule enforcement a political priority. Schools are already adding payment-tracking features to their student systems. Nobody has built the explanation layer, and translation apps do not decode payment slips or their deadlines.
revenue_model: Schools pay ¥300-500 per student per month. Municipalities pay per successful on-time payment or a share of recovered arrears. Employers pay per foreign employee per month. Property managers and guarantors pay per tenant. A small paid human-escalation tier costs the user ¥980 per case.
non_obvious_insight: The failure point is not language in general. It is a single document, the konbini payment slip, and a single hidden rule that its barcode dies on the due date. People miss it by a day and the consequence is a visa problem. The counter clerk sees this daily, so the demand is proven and concentrated. Because the buyer of the outcome is a school or municipality, the paying customer is not the end user.
first_30_days: Build the LINE OA with barcode decoding, OCR and slip-type rules for the five most common slips, and Vietnamese, Nepali and Chinese output reviewed by native speakers. Put QR stickers on the payment counters of my three stores. Pilot with two Osaka language schools, about 300 students, at ¥300 per student per month. Measure on-time payment before and after. Bring the results to one ward's national health insurance department. Partner with an administrative scrivener firm for the escalation tier.

title: Part-Time Seats: Districts Sell Classes to Homeschoolers
one_liner: Software and a playbook that lets shrinking districts enroll homeschoolers and microschoolers a la carte and capture per-pupil funding they are now losing.
customer: Declining-enrollment suburban and rural districts and small charters (superintendents, budget directors) in states that allow part-time or shared-time enrollment.
problem: K-12 enrollment fell from 50.8M to 49.4M (2019-24) and is projected at 46.9M by 2031, with more than 1,000 closures in 2025-26. Districts treat homeschool and microschool families as lost. Yet only about 10% of homeschool families do it K-12 exclusively and 30% do it for 1-2 years (lower-confidence data), so many want labs, band, AP, CTE shops and sports.
solution: A part-time enrollment desk: a catalog of under-filled classes (chem lab, band, welding shop, AP), a family portal for enrollment, records, immunization and attendance, FTE and funding counting per state rules, a la carte billing, and transcript conversion for re-entry. The pitch is that a marginal seat in an empty class costs nearly nothing.
why_now: The enrollment cliff has become a budget crisis. Homeschool ESA families are second-class (Texas homeschoolers get $2,000 against $10,474 for private-school kids), and over 70% of homeschoolers in non-ESA states say they would take public funds. Scholarship-credit and ESA dollars from 2027 can pay for a la carte seats.
revenue_model: $8-25k per year SaaS per district, or a per-enrollment fee of $50-150, or a 5-10% share of incremental revenue.
non_obvious_insight: Districts fight choice by trying to keep full-time kids, but the untapped resource is empty seats in existing classes. Transient and hybrid families are exactly the buyers, and part-time enrollment doubles as a re-entry ramp that brings kids back.
first_30_days: Pick one state with a clear part-time or shared-time statute. Recruit 2 budget-stressed districts for a free pilot. Publish the seat catalog to local homeschool groups. Measure seats sold for the January semester and funding captured.

title: Auto-to-Defense Conversion Accelerator for Tier-2 Suppliers
one_liner: A fixed-price certification package plus matched RFQs that turn idle auto-parts plants into qualified defense and aerospace suppliers.
customer: Tier-2 and tier-3 automotive stampers, machiners and casting shops with 25-250 employees in the Midwest and South. Defense primes co-fund supplier development.
problem: OEM robot orders are down 25% and autos lost 4.5k jobs in August, while defense money is flowing (Hadrian raised $1.37B; it holds an $80M Army deal). Auto suppliers have capacity and process discipline (IATF), but defense work needs AS9100, ITAR registration, DFARS specialty-metals tracking and NIST 800-171 and CMMC Level 2 (phase 2 is scheduled for November 2026). Consultants sell these piecemeal.
solution: A 90-day package: gap assessment, IATF-to-AS9100 crosswalk, ITAR registration, an NIST 800-171 plan on a managed enclave, DFARS specialty-metals tracking, and a mock audit, delivered mostly by templates and a small compliance team. It ends with RFQs matched from primes looking for capacity.
why_now: The auto retreat leaves capacity idle, defense capital is at record levels, and CMMC requirements are phasing in. Primes need more sub-tier suppliers.
revenue_model: $35-80k fixed fee per shop or $3-5k a month for the managed enclave. Success fee on first contract. RFQ-routing fees from primes.
non_obvious_insight: Auto suppliers already have the hard part (process discipline, volume) but are invisible to primes for lack of paperwork. Selling capacity conversion instead of compliance opens the prime's supplier-development budget. The CMMC consultant market is crowded, so the wedge is the RFQ match, not the audit.
first_30_days: Recruit five shops through chambers of commerce, auto-supplier associations and state MEP centers. Partner with a C3PAO and a GCC High MSP. Meet two primes' supplier-development teams about co-funding. Land two paid pilots at about $25k.

title: NFC Open-Item Tags for Aircraft Shift Handover
one_liner: Tamper-evident NFC red-tags that record every opened panel, disconnected line and removed component on an aircraft, and block sign-off until each is closed with an as-left photo.
customer: Directors of maintenance, quality and safety managers at regional airlines, Part 145 shops, Part 135 fleets and helicopter EMS operators. Line stations with 3-6 techs per shift are the beachhead.
problem: The most dangerous moments in line maintenance are shift change and interruption. A tech opens a panel, disconnects a connector or leaves a cap loose, gets pulled to an AOG, and hands over verbally or with a sticky note. The 'system' is a paper red tag, a whiteboard and memory. The 2024 737 MAX 9 door-plug investigation put undocumented removal of fasteners in front of every director of maintenance. Digital task cards do not fix this, because the physical state of the aircraft between task steps is not captured anywhere.
solution: Tamper-evident NFC tags that hang on the physical thing that is open. A tech taps the tag with a phone (offline-first, because hangars have dead zones), records what, why and who, and hangs it. At handover, the app shows a manifest of open tags by tail. The aircraft cannot be released in the app until every tag is closed with an as-left photo. Export goes to the work order as PDF or CSV on day one, and to the maintenance system through an API later. Techs get a time-stamped record of exactly what they did and left.
why_now: The 2024 door-plug event made undocumented maintenance a board-level topic. The FAA's 2024 SMS final rule expanded safety-management obligations to more operators, and safety departments are looking for concrete evidence-capture tools. NFC-capable phones are standard and cheap tags are commodity, so the hardware cost is pennies. AI is a minor part of this, which is a feature. It ships without data-science risk.
revenue_model: Per-aircraft subscription ($75-150 per tail per month) plus consumable tags at $0.50-1.50 each, the razor-and-blade model that made lockout-tagout a large industrial category. Enterprise tier with maintenance-system integration and safety analytics.
non_obvious_insight: Maintenance software dies at the tech's hands, because anything that adds keystrokes gets skipped. This replaces a paper red tag with something faster, and it gives the tech a personal alibi for their own certificate if something is questioned years later. The buyer is quality and safety, not IT, so it needs no integration with the maintenance system to start. Underneath the software is a consumables business.
first_30_days: Ask your own director of maintenance to pilot it at your line station, so you can test it during real shift changes. Build a progressive web app with offline storage and buy 2,000 off-the-shelf NFC stickers. Run a free 30-day pilot at two line stations and one Part 145 shop, then measure tags closed with photo, handover time and missed items caught. Convert the pilot to $99 per tail per month plus tags, and use the measured near-misses as the sales collateral for safety managers.

title: Polling-Agent Payroll With Proof-of-Presence Release
one_liner: Pay each party or observer polling-unit agent directly, releasing money only after a geo-fenced arrival selfie and a result-sheet photo, so nothing gets skimmed on the way down.
customer: Election observer NGOs and civic groups (donor-funded, need audit trails) first. Then campaign directorates of governorship, National Assembly and state assembly candidates across parties. Later, any organisation paying temporary field staff.
problem: Election day is Nigeria's biggest one-day distribution of small payments. Agent allowances travel as lump sums from state to LGA to ward to polling-unit coordinators. Each layer keeps a cut, so a N20k allocation often reaches the agent as N5k. Agents then no-show, or get bought by the other side. Campaign directors know this leakage exists but have no proof and no tool. Since the 2023 cash scarcity, everything has been done by ad-hoc bank transfers and screenshots.
solution: A WhatsApp, USSD and light-Android flow. The party or NGO uploads its INEC-submitted agent list. Each agent gets a wallet or bank payout. Payment is released in tranches: 50% on a geo-fenced 7:30am arrival check-in, 50% on upload of the EC8A result-sheet photo. A coordinator dashboard shows attendance heat-maps and unpaid or unresponsive units in real time. Payments are for presence and documentation only, never for outcomes. Amounts are capped and pre-approved, and a spend report is produced for Electoral Act limits. The platform is strictly non-partisan and serves any party on identical terms.
why_now: INEC has fixed the presidential and National Assembly elections for 16 January 2027 and the governorship and state assembly polls for 6 February 2027. Parties must submit polling-agent names by 10 December 2026 and 6 January 2027. The campaign season is open now, with the Electoral Act 2026 in force. Nigeria has roughly 177,000 polling units, and every serious party wants an agent in each. LLM-based photo checks and cheap bulk-payout APIs (Paystack, Flutterwave, Monnify transfers) make a small team viable. The deadline forces a fast pilot.
revenue_model: 2-3% fee on disbursed allowances, plus a per-agent onboarding fee of about N300-500. Campaigns and NGOs pay a flat SaaS fee for the dashboard and audit pack. Float on pre-funded wallets adds a small yield. After the elections, the same engine is resold as conditional-release payroll for temporary field workers: brand activations, survey and census enumerators, NGO vaccination and outreach drives.
non_obvious_insight: The buyer does not want digital payments. The buyer wants proof that the last person in a 5-layer cash chain actually showed up and got paid. Coordinators lose money to leakage, and that gives campaign principals a reason to bypass the middle layers. The wedge is fraud reduction, not fintech. A conditional-release payment is also more valuable as a workforce-verification product than as a payment product.
first_30_days: Build the check-in and photo flow on top of an existing payout API. Offer it free to one observer NGO or a single state-assembly campaign for a live Ekiti, Osun or by-election dry run, plus a paid pilot for a governorship candidate. Recruit 5 ward coordinators and get 500 agents paid in the first test. Approach NGO election-observation networks and donor programme officers, who already need audit trails. Get written non-partisan and INEC-compliance opinions from a lawyer before the first party contract. Price the first campaign at cost to get case studies.

title: Global Rain Radar From Starlink Dishes
one_liner: Turn opted-in Starlink terminals into the densest rain-gauge network ever built and sell ground-truth rainfall to insurers.
customer: Parametric crop and flood insurers and MGAs, reinsurers, agricultural cooperatives, utilities and municipal flood teams.
problem: Rain gauges are sparse and radar coverage is poor in rural and developing regions. Parametric insurance suffers from basis risk, and disputes arise when the index does not match what happened at the field.
solution: An open-source agent reads a terminal's local signal telemetry, correlates rain-induced attenuation with rain rate, and produces minute-level hyperlocal rainfall. Owners opt in and receive a monthly credit. Sell the result as an API and as audited trigger data for parametric products.
why_now: Starlink reached 12M subscribers, including many rural users. The idea of using satellite-link attenuation as a rain sensor is established in research. Parametric insurance is growing, and public radar and gauge budgets are under pressure.
revenue_model: API subscriptions $20-200k per year per insurer or cooperative. Per-trigger data fees. Owner credits of $2-5 per month as the cost of goods.
non_obvious_insight: Rain fade is a nuisance to network engineers but a measurement to meteorologists. The sensors are already installed and paid for by their owners.
first_30_days: Adapt open-source telemetry tools and recruit 300 terminal owners with a small credit. Co-locate with 30 tipping-bucket gauges and publish a validation note. Pitch two parametric MGAs and one agricultural cooperative, and plan a fallback if SpaceX restricts local access.

title: The 3 A.M. Pharmacist Desk for Konbini
one_liner: A neutral, multilingual, 24-hour remote pharmacist service that issues the emailed certificate the new law will require before konbini without pharmacists can sell OTC drugs.
customer: Convenience-store owners, first independents and multi-chain franchisees in tourist and nightlife areas of Osaka such as Namba, Dotonbori, Shinsekai and Umeda, then chains. Hotels and hostels are a second channel. Stores pay per certificate, or by sharing the margin on OTC sales.
problem: After 11pm, people keep coming in asking for painkillers, stomach medicine, cold medicine, motion-sickness pills, period-pain relief and allergy tablets. Most Type 2 OTC drugs can only be sold when a registered seller is on the premises, and night staff do not have that license. I turn away a steady stream of tourists and night workers every night. Foreign visitors cannot get counseling in their own language even when a pharmacy is open. That is lost margin and a real public-health gap.
solution: Customers scan a QR code on the shelf, choose products, and join a 60-90 second video or chat consultation in Japanese, English, Chinese, Korean or Vietnamese with a licensed pharmacist. They receive a certificate by email or app, and the clerk verifies it on a phone-based web page before ringing up the sale. The pharmacist network is staffed by night-capable remote pharmacists, such as parents and retirees working from home. The operator holds the pharmacy license and takes on regulatory and liability responsibility. Pre-2027, the same desk runs a limited service on quasi-drugs and pharmacy-hours referral lists so the network and the store workflow are ready when the rule takes effect.
why_now: The amended Pharmaceuticals and Medical Devices Act passed in May 2025. It allows convenience stores without pharmacists or registered sellers to sell OTC drugs after the buyer gets an online pharmacist explanation and an emailed certificate. It takes effect around spring 2027. Lawson has said it plans OTC delivery at stores without pharmacists starting in 2026. Inbound tourism to Osaka remains at record levels. The window for a neutral operator is the next 6-9 months, before chains sign exclusive deals.
revenue_model: ¥300-500 per certificate paid by the store, or 25-30% of the OTC gross margin. Hotels and hostels pay a subscription for guest access. Later revenue comes from manufacturers paying for education and sampling inside consultations, and from chains licensing the network.
non_obvious_insight: The bottleneck for konbini OTC is not shelf space, POS integration or the law. It is a supply of licensed humans awake at 3 a.m., speaking Vietnamese or Chinese, who can explain a drug in 90 seconds. Chains will assume they can build this in-house, but they lack pharmacist labor and multilingual night coverage. A neutral network that any owner can join in an afternoon has the advantage, because independent and multi-chain owners have no other option.
first_30_days: Partner with one licensed Osaka pharmacy, or set up the pharmacy entity, and recruit 10-15 remote pharmacists for night and weekend slots. Build the QR, video, certificate and clerk-verification flow as a web app, tested at my three stores on quasi-drugs and referral flow. Pre-sign letters of intent with 10 owners for spring 2027 pricing. Approach two hotels near Namba for guest access. Meet the health-center pharmacy inspection office to confirm the compliance path before launch.

title: Green-Claims Clearance for EU-Bound Brands
one_liner: A crawl-and-fix service that strips or substantiates banned 'eco-friendly' and 'climate-neutral' claims on packaging, product pages and ads for brands selling into the EU.
customer: DTC brands, Amazon and Shopify sellers, and mid-size consumer-goods companies selling to EU consumers, plus their marketing agencies and EU authorised representatives.
problem: Directive (EU) 2024/825 applies from 27 Sept 2026. It bans generic environmental claims ('green', 'eco-friendly') without recognised excellent performance, bans offset-based 'climate neutral' claims, and restricts sustainability labels to certified or public schemes. Small brands have thousands of SKUs of copy across 24 languages and no clear way to check it.
solution: Crawl product pages, packaging PDFs and ad libraries, flag banned and risky patterns in 24 languages, and suggest compliant rewrites with evidence-pack templates (life-cycle summary, certification proof). Add a human legal-review tier and monitoring of competitors' claims for complaint filing.
why_now: The rule began applying on 27 Sept 2026, and member-state transposition laws are now in force. The separate Green Claims Directive was shelved, so consultancies shifted attention, yet this ban is already law and cheap to police by machine.
revenue_model: $1-5k initial audit, $300-1,500 per month monitoring, and agency white-label licences.
non_obvious_insight: This is a deadline-driven, per-SKU checking problem that suits software plus a thin human legal layer, and the first enforcement will often start with competitor complaints. The best lead-gen is showing a brand its own violations.
first_30_days: Build a claims lexicon in five languages. Scan the top 200 product categories on Amazon.de and .fr for violations. Email brand founders their own violations as a free preview. Partner with three EU marketing agencies.

title: Captive Insurer for Hardened Mountain Communities
one_liner: A group cell captive where associations with verified wildfire hardening share first-loss and reinsurance capital.
customer: Condo and townhome associations and mountain-resort communities in California and Colorado with $100K-$1M master premiums, plus their management companies.
problem: Master property premiums have exploded and carriers non-renew whole associations. Reinsurers hold record capital (about $790B, secondary source), yet cannot price unknown community-level risk. Rates fell up to 25% at June 1 2026, but retail carriers pass little through.
solution: A fronted group captive with quota-share reinsurance. Each association's mitigation (IBHS criteria, ember-resistant vents, vegetation plan) is verified and modeled with forward-looking cat models now allowed by California. Members keep the first-loss layer and share the dividends. The first product is captive feasibility plus a verified-hardening scorecard at $15-30K per association, which also improves standard-market placement.
why_now: Howden says reinsurer returns could fall below cost of capital by 2027, so reinsurers want differentiated, verified books now. California's Sustainable Insurance Strategy allows forward-looking models, and Colorado now credits mitigation.
revenue_model: Feasibility fees, then management fees of 8-12% of premium plus ceded profit commission.
non_obvious_insight: The soft reinsurance window is temporary and limited by data quality. Small verified pools can lock multi-year capacity before it hardens.
first_30_days: Meet 3 management companies, score 5 associations, and talk to fronting carriers and captive managers.

title: Cremation Memorial Rooms in Vacant Office Space
one_liner: Pay-per-event celebration-of-life rooms in empty ground-floor and office space for families choosing cremation, with an optional urn-niche wall run through a licensed cemetery partner as the long-term annuity.
customer: Families arranging cremation memorials, and direct-cremation providers and independent funeral homes without a venue. Landlords, lenders and special servicers with vacant space earn a revenue share. A licensed cemetery or church partner operates the niches.
problem: Cremation is about 63% of dispositions and heading to 82% by 2045, so the traditional chapel is redundant, but families still need somewhere to gather and somewhere to keep the ashes. 58% of consumers have attended a service at an unconventional venue, and families pay $2-5K for hotel ballrooms and restaurants. Office vacancy is 17.8% nationally, office CMBS delinquency is 13.2% with $39B maturing within 12 months, and urban cemeteries are out of land.
solution: Lease or license vacant space on short terms and fit it out as a 40-80 seat memorial room with AV for tribute video, catering and celebrant partners. Sell event packages wholesale to direct-cremation and funeral-home partners and directly to families ($1,500-3,500). In phase 2, add a niche wall sold as perpetual-care niches through a licensed cemetery operator, since a niche needs a fraction of the land of a burial plot. Zoning and state cemetery law vary, so licensing runs through the partner.
why_now: Cremation crossed 60% and consumer interest in alternatives is rising. Special servicers of distressed office loans will take short-term income from otherwise dead space. Direct-cremation providers are crowded and need a differentiator beyond price. SCI is growing on pricing while volumes fall, which leaves the low-cost end unserved.
revenue_model: Event fees, wholesale packages for funeral homes and direct-cremation providers, a 10-20% commission or operating share on niche sales, and landlord revenue-share deals. Later, employer celebration-of-life benefits.
non_obvious_insight: Cremation removed the need for the funeral home's most expensive asset, the chapel and its land, but not the human need to gather and to keep remains, which now needs roughly one fiftieth of the space. That makes converted office and retail space, not a cemetery, the right home.
first_30_days: Get a 90-day pop-up license for a vacant ground floor in a mid-size downtown. Sign two celebrants and a caterer. Offer wholesale rates to five direct-cremation providers and run three events at cost. Meet a licensed cemetery operator to scope the niche-wall pilot and the state licensing path.

title: Data Center Deal Desk for Rural Counties
one_liner: An independent negotiating desk that gives county and township boards a benchmark of every comparable data-center abatement and community-benefit contract, a counter term sheet and a fiscal model, paid for by the developer's review escrow.
customer: County commissions, township boards, school boards and local economic-development authorities facing data-center proposals, plus state associations of counties and resident coalitions.
problem: Developers have negotiated dozens of deals and arrive with NDAs and shell LLCs. Counties have negotiated none, and commissioners vote on abatements they can't benchmark. Leverage disappears once approvals are granted. Terms on water use, noise, diesel backup hours, decommissioning bonds, grid-cost protection and clawbacks vary wildly.
solution: Parse every signed abatement, PILOT, host-community and large-load utility agreement obtainable (the Federation of American Scientists started collecting signed agreements in early 2026, and public records requests fill gaps) into a comparable clause database. Deliver a two-week Deal Review: where each term falls against the median and best deals, a counter term sheet, fiscal, water and power impact modeling, and a 'second chair' during meetings. Fees are typically recoverable from the applicant through a third-party review escrow.
why_now: The 2026 data-center land rush has local governments scrambling: most local ordinances and ballot measures tracked in 2026 passed, many deals sit behind NDAs, and counties from Texas to Ohio are tabling or denying abatements while others approve blind. LLMs make reading hundreds of messy contracts cheap. Incumbent consultants and county attorneys don't have a comparables dataset.
revenue_model: $12k to $40k per deal review (billed to the developer's review escrow where the county allows it), annual data license for state county associations ($30k to $100k) and, later, a pre-vetted 'fast-lane' term sheet that developers pay to use.
non_obvious_insight: Information asymmetry, not law, is the county's problem, and the cheapest fix is a set of comparables. Commissioners also fear being first or being fleeced, so 'we asked for what the median county got' gives political cover. Charging the applicant through the review escrow means the buyer, a cash-strapped county, doesn't need a budget line.
first_30_days: Collect 100 signed agreements from the FAS repository, Texas Chapter 312 filings and records requests, and code them into a comparison table. Publish free state scorecards. Email commissioners in counties with pending abatement votes and offer a $5k rapid clause redline, asking the county to request that the developer pay under its review-fee ordinance.

title: Costly-Commitment Kits for Fitness Congregations
one_liner: A retention product for boutique gyms and run clubs that borrows religion's real community mechanism, costly commitment, to turn members into a congregation.
customer: Owners of boutique fitness studios, CrossFit boxes, climbing gyms and multi-site run clubs, with franchisors as the scale channel.
problem: Gen Z made up 47% of new gym joins in 2025 yet posts the highest churn (around 54% in one industry dataset), and nearly half of them say community is why they stay. Studios respond with discounts, apps and easier joining, which attracts free-riders and does not build attachment.
solution: A kit of printed rites, a coach's liturgy guide and light software: an initiation for a founding cohort, attendance vows made to a partner, earned 'colors' for milestones, a dawn 'vigil' class, rites for return-from-injury and for a member's death, and a warm leaving ritual. We A/B the kit across studios against controls on 90-day retention.
why_now: ABC Fitness's 2025 year-end report shows Gen Z dominating new joins and community as a top reason to stay. Run clubs and studios are already positioned as a substitute for church, and retention is the KPI that owners pay to move.
revenue_model: $199-499 per month per studio for the kit and software, a performance option of about 10% of measured retention gains, and licensing to franchisors across their locations.
non_obvious_insight: The whole industry builds community by removing friction, while religious sociology (Iannaccone's 'Why Strict Churches Are Strong') finds that commitment, sacrifice and visible costs create strong communities and free-rider filters. Add cost that feels like meaning (time, visibility, obligation) instead of a fee and members become attached, so the friction studios fear is the mechanism.
first_30_days: Recruit five studios from one local franchise. Run a founding-cohort covenant for new joiners and compare 90-day retention against control cohorts. Publish the result and pitch it to franchise developers.

title: Public-Access TV Stations Become Media Notaries
one_liner: Convert struggling PEG community-media centers into witnessed-recording and signing hubs that cities pay to certify official meeting video and creators pay to prove a recording was performed live by a human in a real room.
customer: City and county clerks ($300-600/month for signed, canonical video of meetings, hearings and emergency briefings), PEG access centers (keep about 60% as delivery partners), and local musicians, podcasters and hyperlocal news creators ($45 per witnessed session or $15/month for verified-clip embeds). Later buyers are sync buyers and ad agencies.
problem: PEG centers (public, educational and government access TV) are funded by cable franchise fees that erode as cable subscriptions fall (prior knowledge), yet they own studios, gear, staff and a role recording local government. Meanwhile fully AI tracks passed 50% of Deezer uploads (July 2026), AI-cloned officials' clips circulate, platform human badges are free and per-artist (Spotify) or absent (YouTube will not demote labeled AI), and detectors are only probabilistic. Nobody sells 'this was made live, in this room, on this date, witnessed by a public institution'.
solution: A roughly $600 witness kit plus software: hardware-signed capture into C2PA manifests, staff-attested session logs with an ID check of performers, and raw timestamped multitrack takes. Cities get a canonical signed meeting archive and a public 'verify this clip' page. Local news creators embed verified clips, and artists attach a 'Recorded live at [Center], [date]' credential to releases and distributor metadata.
why_now: EU AI Act Article 50 marking and disclosure duties started applying 2026-08-02. C2PA 2.3 and TikTok's July 2026 steering-committee entry mean signed media can now travel across platforms. Platforms went from tolerating to policing AI in months (Bandcamp ban, Spotify AI Persona labels, TIDAL demonetization), and PEG funding pressure means centers need new revenue lines.
revenue_model: City subscriptions, per-session fees split with PEG centers, an annual software license to centers, and later per-clip verification fees from sync buyers.
non_obvious_insight: A credential is only as trustworthy as the institution behind it. Platforms cannot referee because they sell AI tools, and detectors give probabilities while a witness gives testimony. PEG centers are the only neutral, government-adjacent, physically distributed and already-recording institutions in most towns, and their core asset is exactly what provenance lacks: a place and a person willing to attest.
first_30_days: Contact the Alliance for Community Media state chapters and equip 3 PEG stations in one state. Sign one month of council meetings free, then demo a deepfaked council clip against the signed original to sell a $300/month city plan. Open 'Witnessed Live' studio hours to 20 local artists at $45.

title: GLP-1 Menu Labeling Layer for Independent Restaurants
one_liner: A cheap per-dish protein, fiber and portion labeling and half-portion pricing tool that tells the 12% of diners on GLP-1 drugs which dishes fit, published wherever they look.
customer: Owner-operated independent restaurants and small groups (2-30 locations), plus campus and hospital cafeterias, that sell through delivery apps and Google Maps. They pay $199 setup and $39/month.
problem: About 11-12% of US adults now take GLP-1 drugs, up from 3% in 2024 (KFF poll). Chains have reacted with lighter-portion sections, protein menus and dedicated GLP-1 menus (Olive Garden, Shake Shack, Chipotle, Subway, Smoothie King). Independents have no dietitian, no nutrition data and no way to show which dishes fit. Their menus say nothing about protein grams or half sizes, and independents are exempt from chain menu-labeling rules.
solution: The owner uploads a menu PDF or photo. The tool estimates per-dish calories, protein and fiber as a range, using LLM recipe parsing plus USDA FoodData Central. It tags dishes 'protein-first' or 'light plate' using explicit, published thresholds. It suggests a half-portion or 'box half before it reaches the table' price point that keeps margin (food cost is typically about 30% of price, so a half portion at 65-70% of price holds gross profit). It then auto-publishes to the Google Business Profile menu, DoorDash and Uber Eats descriptions, a QR menu and printable table tents, with a short staff script. All output is worded as an estimate with no medical claims.
why_now: Health-topic search data shows GLP1 at 1.5M monthly searches (+1,011%) and Fibremaxxing +7,900%, and Google's Summergeist report shows fibermaxxing at an all-time high. Chains are now marketing to this group in 2026, so independents are losing a segment that dines out often.
revenue_model: $199 setup, $39/month per location for menu updates, delivery-app syncing and 'reorder tag' analytics. Add-ons: $99 printed table tents and $149 chef-recipe reformulation consult. Later: bundle through POS resellers, delivery-marketing agencies and restaurant associations.
non_obvious_insight: The gap is communication, not the menu. A 2026 survey cited by ABC News found 89% of GLP-1 users wish restaurants 'communicated better about options that promote health and wellness' while 90% say restaurants typically do offer healthy items. The same coverage cites a National Restaurant Association survey that GLP-1 users make 7.6 restaurant purchases a week versus 5.1 for non-users. They want 'half-sized and lunch-sized portions, protein-first options... the ability to box food before it reaches the table' (https://abcnews.com/US/weight-loss-drug-usage-grows-restaurants-offer-glp/story?id=135711648). So the cheapest fix is labeling and relabeling what a kitchen already makes, not building new dishes, and nutrition-lab analysis is unnecessary. Chain moves are documented at https://www.foodingredientsfirst.com/news/glp-1-friendly-menus-food-dining-2026.html and https://www.nbcnews.com/news/us-news/smaller-portions-protein-glp-1s-are-quietly-changing-chain-restaurant-rcna254178, which both say nothing about independents, so that segment is unserved. Search demand: https://explodingtopics.com/health-topics.
first_30_days: Days 1-7: build the menu parser, estimates and tag thresholds, and have a registered dietitian review the method and disclaimers. Days 8-20: walk into 30 independent restaurants in one dense neighborhood with a free 'GLP-1 menu scorecard' on their own menu, and pitch via the local restaurant association and Toast/Square consultants. Days 21-30: onboard 8-10 paying restaurants, publish updated Google Business Profile and delivery listings, and track half-portion attach rate and new-visitor searches for a case study.

title: Crop Scouts of the Sea for Seafood Buyers
one_liner: A paid panel of working skippers and tender operators that texts in daily run, quality and delivery-limit data, sold to seafood buyers and lenders days to weeks before the market sees it.
customer: Wild-salmon importers and distributors, club-store and retail category buyers, Japanese and European trading houses, canned and frozen sockeye brokers, banks lending to processors, reinsurers and commodity funds. Each pays $10-30K/year. Panelists are paid, so fishermen are also customers of the cash flow.
problem: Bristol Bay is the source of most of the world's wild sockeye, and price went from $1.03/lb avg in 2025 (41.2M fish) to $1.72/lb in 2026 (30.1M fish). Farmed Atlantic salmon has futures and analyst coverage. Wild sockeye has neither. Buyers see ADF&G escapement and harvest counts and press releases, but not fish size, color, quality, roe, which processors are on delivery limits, tender backlogs, or which plants are paying up for fish. That information reaches the market 2-4 weeks late, after forward prices are already set.
solution: Recruit 150-300 skippers, crew and tender operators. Each sends a 60-second daily check-in (pounds per boat, average fish weight, limit status by processor, hours waiting at the tender, water temp, color and quality, weather, gear). Validate it against ADF&G counts and AIS. Publish a daily 'Fisher's Report' with the run-timing curve, quality and limit maps, and proprietary indexes, plus a weekly call with a retired skipper as analyst. Extend to Copper River, Prince William Sound, Kodiak and Southeast.
why_now: The one-year 67% swing in average price has made buyers and lenders hungry for earlier signals. Alt-data buyers already pay for crop scouts and satellite counts in other commodities. Starlink on boats makes real-time reporting possible. LLMs can clean messy text reports into structured data at almost no cost.
revenue_model: Subscriptions of $12-30K/year per company, custom data feeds at $50K+, and analyst calls. Pay panelists $150-400 per season out of 20-30% of revenue. Add other fisheries and other 'boots on the ground' sectors later.
non_obvious_insight: Information in the fleet moves at VHF speed. The whole fleet knows the run is late, the fish are small, or the tenders are backed up days before any official number, and buyers treat it as noise. Skippers will happily share anonymized volume and quality data if you pay them, because it does not touch their contract terms or fishing spots. The valuable part is aggregation and a track record. Keep panelists' data separate from any confidential processor contract terms, and get securities and antitrust counsel before selling to funds.
first_30_days: Recruit 40 panelists from Facebook groups and associations while everyone is idle after settlements. Ask them for 2026 season logs (many keep daily notes and fish tickets). Backtest against ADF&G data and the 2026 price path, and show the panel's signals would have led the market. Send a sample '2026 in hindsight' report to 30 importers and analysts. Aim for 3 pilot subscriptions at about $5K each before the May opener.

title: Sell Heat Pumps to Health Plans
one_liner: Sell home electrification to Medicaid and Medicare Advantage plans as a cost-of-care reduction instead of selling it to homeowners as a climate upgrade.
customer: Medicaid managed-care organizations, Medicare Advantage plans (supplemental benefits) and nonprofit hospital community-benefit budgets. They pay per completed install, plus an outcome bonus.
problem: The 25C credit ended 12/31/2025, homeowners face ~$9,000 heat pump quotes, and HEAR rebates roll out unevenly by state. Meanwhile health plans pay for asthma and COPD ER visits, heat illness and gas-stove-related respiratory events that cost thousands per admission.
solution: A 'clinical electrification program in a box'. Claims data finds members with asthma, COPD or heat vulnerability. A vetted contractor network installs a heat pump, heat pump water heater or induction cooktop. The program stacks HEAR/HOMES rebates so the plan pays only the gap, tracks ER visits and medication use, and reports ROI to the plan. Billing runs through Medicaid health-related-social-needs and in-lieu-of-service pathways or MA supplemental benefits.
why_now: Some state Medicaid waivers (Oregon's climate-device benefit) and MA plans already pay for air conditioners and air filtration. $8.8B of HEAR/HOMES money needs matching demand. Federal homeowner credits are gone, so the old buyer has weakened.
revenue_model: $2-6k net per install paid by the plan after rebate stacking, a platform fee, contractor take-rate, and outcome-based bonuses.
non_obvious_insight: Insiders keep trying to improve the homeowner's payback. The payer with the fastest ROI is the one who pays for ambulances. Health plans have budget lines, claims data to find the right homes, and no need for a 10-year payback.
first_30_days: Pick one state with a Medicaid climate-device benefit or a Southwest MA plan. Find two MCO community-health leads. Build claims-based targeting analytics. Run a 25-home pilot with one contractor using existing HEAR or utility rebates, and write a one-page ROI memo from baseline ER usage.

title: License-in-a-Box for Insourcing Property Owners
one_liner: A licensed managing-broker entity, trust-account oversight and compliance layer that lets owners run AI-native property management in-house without building licensing state by state.
customer: Institutional owners, family offices, search-fund operators and AI-native property-ops startups with 500-10,000 units that want to insource management.
problem: Owners are insourcing to capture AI efficiency and stop paying a percentage-of-rent fee (T2 Capital's Base Living launched with 24 site associates and 8 corporate staff across three states). Most states require a licensed broker of record, trust accounts, fair-housing controls and E&O cover, and each new state costs months of licensing and hires.
solution: A licensed entity in 20+ states supervises the owner's own operation: trust-accounting oversight integrated with Yardi, AppFolio and Entrata, monthly reconciliations, fair-housing and fee-law compliance, E&O coverage and regulator liaison. Owners run day-to-day operations with their own AI stack.
why_now: The insourcing wave is underway, third-party manager incentives are misaligned, and the fee and pricing-law patchwork is raising compliance load.
revenue_model: $1.50-3.50 per unit per month plus a $10-25K onboarding fee per state, and an E&O program revenue share.
non_obvious_insight: The barrier to AI-native operations is not software but a licensed human of record in every state, which is cheap to rent and expensive to build. Incumbent managers will not sell it because it undermines their fee model.
first_30_days: Form the entity with a multi-state-licensed broker and counsel. Sign two owners with 500-2,000 units in one or two states as reduced-rate design partners. Get an E&O quote and publish a free state-by-state licensing matrix as a lead magnet.

title: Sold-Out-of-Trust Radar for Floorplan Lenders
one_liner: Catch dealers that sell floored cars and pocket the payoff by watching the one signal an F&I insider knows can't be hidden: the VIN disappears from public listings but the floorplan payoff never arrives.
customer: Floorplan lenders and their auditors: independent floorplan companies, captive finance arms, regional banks and credit unions with dealer lines, and warehouse lenders that fund subprime and buy-here-pay-here dealers. Pay $15 to $30 per monitored dealer per month plus enterprise data fees.
problem: A dealer sells out of trust when it sells a floored car and does not pay the lender's payoff on time. It is how small cash squeezes become fraud. Ford and Stellantis are in court against Sky Auto Mall over exactly this, and floorplan use is heavier with inventory at roughly 88 days' supply and rates at SOFR plus 200 to 400 bps. Lenders police it with periodic on-site audits (monthly, quarterly or random), so a dealer can sell for weeks before anyone looks. The dealer's own delay makes it worse, since contracts in transit stretch to a week or more before the lender funds, so honest and dishonest dealers look identical in the books.
solution: Daily VIN-level monitoring of each lender's floored inventory against public and licensed listing feeds from the dealer's site and the major marketplaces. When a floored VIN disappears from listings, the tool starts a clock. It cross-checks against lender-provided payoff events and, where available, title and registration transactions and electronic lien releases. If no payoff shows within the expected window (about 7 to 10 days for a clean deal, longer for slow lenders), it flags the dealer and VIN and ranks risk by dealer history and how many VINs are in the queue. Flags trigger a spot audit or a curtailment call. A dealer-facing version shows honest dealers exactly which VINs look 'unpaid' so they can fix processing before the lender calls, and it doubles as an early-warning feed for warehouse lenders.
why_now: Sept 2025's Tricolor and PrimaLend collapses put double-pledged collateral and verification failures in front of every subprime lender and their investors. In March 2026 Ford and Stellantis were still litigating floorplan fraud against Sky Auto Mall. Rising inventory and higher rates increase floorplan reliance. Public listing feeds and cheap LLM data extraction make VIN-level monitoring practical for a team of three.
revenue_model: Per-dealer monthly monitoring fee, a per-alert fee on confirmed cases, and enterprise data licensing to captives and ABS or warehouse investors. Upsell: a contracts-in-transit tracker that gives dealers a lender-verified funding timeline and later powers same-day advances against verified contracts.
non_obvious_insight: The only place SOT cannot hide is the retail listing. A dealer will lie about payoffs, backdate titles and pay one lender with another's money, but it still has to take a car off its website when it sells it, because customers and marketplaces punish stale listings. Auditors check what is on the lot; nobody checks what left the internet. An F&I person knows this from watching sold cars vanish from the site the same day the deal is signed, and from knowing how long a funded payoff should really take.
first_30_days: Build a scraper for a pilot set of 50 dealer inventory pages and a listing-history log. Backtest on cases visible in public court filings (the Sky Auto Mall filings and a handful of others) to show the signal would have fired weeks earlier. Approach three small independent floorplan lenders and two credit unions with dealer floorplan lines, offer a free 60-day pilot on their books, and charge $20 per dealer per month after proving at least one real catch.

title: Pre-Permitted Gateway Campuses for Satellite Constellations
one_liner: A real-estate developer for multi-tenant satellite gateway sites with power, fiber, interference studies and landing-right support.
customer: Constellation operators (broadband, direct-to-cell, EO downlink) that need dozens of gateways in many countries, and ground-station-as-a-service providers.
problem: Every constellation needs gateways that are radio-quiet, low in rain fade, and connected to fiber and power. Zoning, community opposition and national landing rights make site acquisition slow, and launching more satellites does not help if gateways are the bottleneck. AST is launch-constrained now, but ground capacity is next.
solution: Option, entitle and pre-permit 'gateway campuses' in strategic regions, then lease antenna pads on 10-15 year terms. Include interference and rain-fade studies, fiber and power, and local licensing help. Start in the Caribbean, Latin America and Africa, where landing rights and site scarcity bind hardest.
why_now: Launch capacity is exploding, so the bottleneck shifts to the ground. Spectrum is now owned by operators with big plans (SpaceX, AT&T, AST). Direct-to-cell needs many gateways to reach many carriers.
revenue_model: Pad leases $8-25k per month per antenna. Development fee on entitlement assignment. Long-term power and fiber pass-through margin.
non_obvious_insight: Operators over-invest in satellites and under-invest in the boring ground sites that gate capacity. Zoning boards, not rockets, may be the binding constraint.
first_30_days: Use GIS to shortlist 30 parcels near fiber and power across five regions. Take low-cost options on five. Get LOIs from two gateway-hungry operators or teleport providers before spending on entitlements.

title: Exoskeletons That Delay Tradesperson Retirement
one_liner: Lease passive and powered exoskeletons with fitting, coaching and outcome-based pricing to shops and insurers, targeting 55+ tradespeople whose retirement drives the labor gap.
customer: Workers' comp carriers and PEOs, contractor associations, and 10-100 employee roofing, plumbing, HVAC, framing and drywall shops with aging crews.
problem: ABC says most of the 349K 2026 shortfall is retirements, and older tradespeople leave over knees, backs and shoulders. Replacement hiring is impossible in a market where trade-school enrollment hype is called a demographic mirage. Strain injuries also drive comp claims.
solution: Vetted kits (passive shoulder and back supports, emerging powered hip and knee assists), professional fitting, a task playbook for overhead, attic, roofing and crawlspace work, and usage and injury-risk telemetry. Monthly lease with a guarantee tied to comp premium reduction or absence rates, piloted with carriers first.
why_now: Powered assist suits have fallen from tens of thousands of dollars to low thousands per unit. Comp carriers face margin pressure and want proven loss-control tools. The retirement wave now dominates the labor gap, and hiring cannot fill it.
revenue_model: $150-300 per worker per month lease, a carrier program fee, and outcome-based rebates.
non_obvious_insight: This is a retention and insurance business, not a robotics business: the cheapest new journeyman is the 62-year-old who did not retire. The buyer with the incentive and the loss data is the comp carrier, not the worker or the owner.
first_30_days: Approach two regional comp carriers or PEOs with a 60-day pilot. Sign three shops (10 workers total) and measure discomfort, absences and adoption. Secure wholesale terms with one exoskeleton supplier and one trade association endorsement.

title: Multi-Rail Cash-Flow Underwriting After UPI Fees
one_liner: When UPI stops being free for big tickets, reconstruct small-merchant revenue from GST, bank and supplier data instead of UPI alone.
customer: NBFCs, small finance banks and cash-flow lenders that lend to kirana and small retail businesses.
problem: Lenders assumed UPI data was the universal truth for underwriting. The Oct 15 MDR (0.4% above Rs 2,000, capped at Rs 300) hits about 4% of P2M volume but about 66% of value, so merchants now have a reason to route big tickets through cash or bank transfer.
solution: An API that combines Account Aggregator bank data, GST e-invoice and filing data, supplier invoices and soundbox/QR data into a revenue estimate with a rail-shift adjustment. The wedge is a turnover sanity-check score for five NBFCs.
why_now: MDR starts Oct 15, the Supreme Court refused a stay, and retailers are organising protests. RBI's cash-flow lending push depends on this data.
revenue_model: Rs 40-120 per scored application plus a monitoring fee on the live loan book.
non_obvious_insight: A fee on exactly the high-value 66% creates an incentive to hide it. The rail shift is a data-quality shock, and the first lender to model it gets an underwriting edge.
first_30_days: Get consented data on about 200 existing borrowers from one NBFC partner and backtest against repayments. Offer a 60-day free pilot.

title: Condo Vote Toolkit for Tourist-Flat Bans
one_liner: A compliant e-vote, notice and evidence kit that lets condo communities decide the fate of tourist flats building by building, sold to the property administrators who run those votes.
customer: Property administrators who manage 50-300 buildings each (administradores de fincas in Spain, condominium managers in Brazil) and other managers in cities with short-term-rental limits. Later, mid-term-let operators and hosts who need a 'yes' vote (a firewalled second product).
problem: Tourism regulation is moving from city hall to the building's owners' assembly. Brazil (May 2026) requires 2/3 condo-owner approval, Madrid bans listings without a private entrance, and Barcelona bans all short-term rentals from Nov 2028 (Palma already has a full ban). Spain's 2025 condo-law change also gave owner communities a say over tourist flats (from my knowledge, verify locally). Each vote needs proper notice, quorum, minutes and bylaw amendments. Administrators run this on paper and email, and challenged votes get annulled on procedure.
solution: A per-building workspace with a jurisdiction-specific notice-and-quorum engine, proof of delivery, proxy voting, minutes generation, and local-language bylaw templates approved by local counsel. It adds an incident log (noise, keys, trash) with timestamped evidence and standard letters, plus a 'what is still allowed' guide for converting to compliant mid-term leases.
why_now: Bans and consent rules landing in 2025-2026 force thousands of building-level decisions in the next 12-24 months. Spain's $75M fine on Airbnb (Dec 2025) shows enforcement is real. Stranded short-stay inventory means every owner must choose between a ban and conversion.
revenue_model: About EUR 149 per vote packet, or EUR 2 per unit per month for administrator firms. A separate host-side package (consent-campaign management) at about EUR 500 per approved building, kept firewalled from the neutral tool.
non_obvious_insight: The fight over overtourism has moved to the general assembly of a single building. The buyer who feels the pain is the administrator exposed when a vote is challenged, and no legal-tech vendor sells to these mostly paper-based professionals.
first_30_days: Start with Spain. Build the vote checklist, notice templates and minutes generator in spreadsheets and documents. Offer them to 10 administrators in Barcelona, Madrid and Valencia via the professional-college newsletter at EUR 149 per vote, and aim for 5 paid votes. Automate whichever step they complain about most.

title: City Micro-Rule API for Group Tour Operators
one_liner: A continuously updated database of group caps, loudspeaker rules, coach drop-off bans, fees and overnight-parking bans across overtouristed places, delivered as an itinerary checker for tour operators and campervan renters.
customer: Small and mid-size group tour operators, DMCs, shore-excursion companies, guide associations and campervan or RV rental firms in Europe.
problem: Cities answer overtourism with many small rules, such as group-size caps and loudspeaker bans in places like Venice and Amsterdam, plus coach access fees and wild-camping bans elsewhere. These live in local-language ordinances, and fines fall on operators and guides. Nobody publishes a single source of truth.
solution: Use multilingual LLM ingestion of municipal ordinances with human legal review for the top 60 cities. The product is an itinerary checker that flags violations and fees, a weekly change digest, an API for booking systems and a WhatsApp bot for guides.
why_now: Municipal crackdowns keep multiplying (Barcelona, Palma, Venice, Amsterdam, the Balearics, Glasgow's levy from Jan 2027). Long-context LLMs make parsing ordinances in many languages cheap only recently.
revenue_model: USD 79-299 per month per operator, enterprise API licences for cruise lines and campervan renters, and paid city packs.
non_obvious_insight: Overtourism policy has fragmented into thousands of tiny local rules. The pain is compliance risk rather than any single rule, and every new rule makes the product more valuable.
first_30_days: Curate rules for 10 cities (for example Venice, Rome, Florence, Amsterdam, Barcelona, Dubrovnik, Lisbon, Athens, Edinburgh and Kyoto) with local guides. Sell 10 operators at USD 99 per month through guide associations, and publish free rules-by-city pages for SEO lead generation.
